current_contract_findings.finding: v1 origin and code_locator require a 40-character lowercase commit, one portable path, one inspected manifest, one source_id, and a line-snippet SHA-256 that resolves against the captured bytes. The common.v1 code_locator and code-evidence-manifest.v1 schema therefore cannot carry a 64-character Git SHA-256 object ID, tree/blob proof, mode, or Git type.
current_contract_findings.consequence: Never widen v1 regexes or overwrite an old manifest. A SHA-256 Git repository or any target needing tree/blob/mode proof requires the v2 manifest and locator below.

current_contract_findings.finding: _code accepts exactly manifest/repo_record/alignment, requires an inspected v1 manifest to match the repo_record canonical repository/commit and alignment officiality/license, and emits one wiki/code/<repo_page_slug>.md page. stage_compilation at 189-199 is explicitly preview-only.
current_contract_findings.consequence: Do not feed a v2 relation into legacy._code or treat stage_compilation as a publication receipt. Add a separate v2 adapter and retain legacy page bytes.

current_contract_findings.finding: The v2 compiler validates complete paper source associations/raw/extraction/head/receipt/registration sets, but its code loop still calls legacy._code at 242-243 and paper links still derive from repo_record.paper_ids at 251-256.
current_contract_findings.consequence: The minimum integration is a v2 code relation group and page adapter in the source-aware compiler. Legacy code groups remain accepted unchanged; v2 pages must carry their own relation identity and never silently replace a prior repo page.

current_contract_findings.finding: The current staged capture validates a proposal, retained prepared/plan/blob paths, one batch/session, pinned transaction inspect, and capture source_id. It produces content capture, not Git commit/tree/blob or officiality proof.
current_contract_findings.consequence: A v2 handoff must carry the observation's same-session complete-set and Git facts into v2 manifests. It may reuse the existing .raw/captured/<payload-sha>.bin/.blob bytes and transaction inspection, but cannot upgrade caller-declared origin facts by itself.

current_contract_findings.finding: The current semantic prefixes and schema registry admit only v1 code manifests/alignment manifests. _legacy_artifacts requires each manifest's actual capture and code source-ledger row; _code_groups requires exactly one v1 manifest and alignment per repo commit; _locators resolves only an actual inspected v1 manifest and rejects repository Markdown evidence; collect_source_state requires receipt-backed ledger snapshots and exact rendered pages; preserve_history protects existing repo/source/claim/page identities.
current_contract_findings.consequence: Add explicit v2 roles and complete-set checks rather than broadening v1 patterns. Existing repo records, source rows, receipts, pages, and locators remain immutable.

current_contract_findings.finding: _prospective validates the exact payload overlay and source-history rules before collect_source_state; _transport_limits constructs the next ingest receipt/head/bundle bounds; prepare_source_publication and inspect_source_publication re-audit the retained Vault, recheck basis, assemble the shared transaction, and bind the complete read set.
current_contract_findings.consequence: Code evidence, source-ledger registration, relation/config/capability records, and versioned compiled pages must enter one source-publication payload/receipt. No direct Vault write or separate unbound code publication is acceptable.

current_contract_findings.finding: The source catalog re-audits current state, reconstructs exact rows, installs only a .work cache, and requires canonical ordering/self-digests. Existing code evidence resolution requires one v1 manifest and exact line bytes.
current_contract_findings.consequence: Keep source-catalog-v1 and its keys/resources byte-compatible. Introduce a source-catalog-v2 profile/contract and explicit v2 relation/manifests/config/capability rows; add a v2 locator resolver without changing v1 resolution.

current_contract_findings.finding: audit_integrity replays the complete receipt chain, current managed paths, ever-claimed raw paths, orphans, and optional runtime correlation. Backup requires receipt-backed truth and exact raw complete-set coverage anchored to the head receipt; archive and restore revalidate the embedded manifest. Restore verification currently checks the legacy catalog/runtime path.
current_contract_findings.consequence: Every new raw capture must be a receipt write or a valid captured raw claim, every semantic v2 artifact must be a receipt write, and restore verification must invoke the v2 catalog/relation closure before accepting a restored tree.

consumed_unchanged.binding: One paper_id, optional exact source association reference, one canonical repository, one full commit/object format, explicit bounded role/path set, complete budgets, and canonical request digest. This is the R1 observation request; do not infer a new path or commit from a display head.

One retained connector/session lineage, one repository/commit/tree, every requested target retained including missing/inaccessible/unsafe states, and a complete observation hash. A normalized-only target is not raw Git authority.

One handoff per present raw target. Carry observation_id, request_sha256, repository, object format, commit/tree/path/mode/git_type/blob_oid, raw and normalized hashes, capture proposal and source-file identity. A multi-file observation is the shared lineage container, not a merged manifest.

new_successor_schemas.purpose: Capture manifest for a verified raw handoff when v1 cannot represent the Git object identity.
rules: Accept sha1/40 or sha256/64 commit_oid only according to git_object_format.
Keep Git blob_oid separate from ordinary raw_sha256 and normalized_sha256.
Require exact path/mode/type and same observation commit/tree for every member of a relation.
Bind stored raw bytes through the existing capture identity and source-ledger code row.
A v2 manifest cannot be projected into a v1 locator by truncation, rehashing, or guessed commit text.

new_successor_schemas.purpose: Exact source citation for v2 code bytes, including object-format/tree/blob and handoff identity.
rules: Resolve only against the one named v2 manifest and exact stored raw bytes.
Retain one logical locator per requested path even when duplicate files have equal bytes.
Keep v1 common.code_locator untouched for accepted historical 40-hex evidence.

new_successor_schemas.purpose: Data-only parser result for an explicitly observed configuration target.
rules: Only the frozen closed JSON/TOML profile is eligible unless a separately accepted profile is named.
Reject imports, includes, tags, anchors, constructors, interpolation, scripts, callables, duplicate-key ambiguity, model loading, and parser limits without execution.
Config evidence may support a capability proposal but never establishes officiality or checkpoint artifact verification.

new_successor_schemas.purpose: Versioned capability evidence and bounded absence record.
rules: Use training, inference, data, evaluation, or checkpoints with present/absent/partial/unverified status.
Present/partial claims need v2 locator or an explicitly marked README-only observation; absence requires observed inventory, commit/tree scope, patterns and inventory digest.
Checkpoint URL/revision/license metadata may be retained without downloading weights; artifact_verified requires exact observed artifact evidence.

new_successor_schemas.purpose: Immutable independent review of paper-to-repository officiality and evidence gaps.
rules: Signals A-D retain exact source refs, observed version/commit, line/excerpt locator and source hash.
Only an authorized independent human/relation reviewer can issue official/unofficial/unverified_candidate/evidence_insufficient.
A/B plus C is preferred evidence, not an automatic formula; same organization, name similarity, dependency/baseline, or model suggestion is insufficient.

new_successor_schemas.purpose: Canonical successor join consumed by source-aware publication/compiler/catalog.
rules: source_association is an exact association_id plus association_sha256 from source_versions, not a mutable current display head.
All refs are content-addressed, all manifests/handoffs form one complete target set, and review decision is copied only after independent review.
page_path must be a portable versioned wiki/code path; use a relation-specific path such as wiki/code/<repo_page_slug>/<relation_sha256>.md when an older page already exists.
relation_sha256 covers the complete canonical relation and cannot be edited in place.

successor_contracts.record_path_policy: These successor artifacts remain under .raw/derived content-addressed namespaces until source_state role patterns, receipt closure, catalog projection, backup, and restore verification are implemented and accepted together. Do not place them in legacy repo-record.v1/alignment-manifest.v1 slots or mutate v1 files.

receipt_backed_join.single_transaction_rule: A code publication is one source-publication prepare/inspect transaction containing the new raw capture writes or valid captured-input claims, v2 manifests, observation/handoff/config/capability/review/relation artifacts, any new source-ledger snapshot and source-ledger bytes, and the versioned compiled page set.
prepare_phase: Validate every successor document before acquiring current-state authority, exactly as source_publication.prepare_source_publication does at lines 240-250.

Retain one _Snapshot and audited current state. Recompute the complete prospective overlay and reject immutable replacements, duplicate source IDs, duplicate paths/digests, incomplete target sets, stale association refs, and page collisions.

For each new code raw path, require a source-ledger row with origin={kind:file,locator:<captured path>}, content_kind=code, content_sha256=raw SHA-256, a new source_id, and the exact generated ledger snapshot. Preserve the old source-ledger snapshot when replacing the ledger, as required by source_publication.py:172-179 and source_state.py:554-557.

Include all code raw captures in the receipt's claimed_inputs only when they are existing captured paths with the exact payload digest; semantic v2 records are transaction writes. Do not invent a claimed input for an unobserved .raw/derived path.

Use the existing ingest receipt/head/bundle size proof. The operation must have a distinct batch and operation identity from the observation/capture operation, matching the existing registration distinction at source_publication.py:75-93.
inspect_phase: Reaudit the same Vault, require the request basis and prospective inventory digest to match, and retain the complete read set before constructing the shared transaction, following source_publication.py:290-331.

Require transaction business writes to equal the exact v2 overlay and read preconditions to equal every current non-write path. Bind the external operation result with operation_result.bind_operation_result when an upstream runtime result is supplied.
Only after complete relation review and source joins pass may the relation be included in canonical page/catalog input. A prepared proposal is not publication authority.
audit_requirements: audit_integrity must replay all receipts, verify the head and receipt digests, reject unreachable receipts, compare the complete managed path set, preserve every ever-claimed raw capture, and report orphan captured files; see receipt_audit.py:314-363.
A code relation with no receipt write, no source-ledger binding, or an orphan capture is invalid even if its JSON self-hash is correct.
No source publication function may write the real Vault directly; only the accepted upstream transaction applies inspected writes after the external human/system gate.

compiler_and_page_integration.legacy_preservation: Leave canonical_compiler._code and canonical_compiler.compile_pages unchanged for v1 inputs. Legacy repo-record.v1 and paper-code-alignment.v1 continue to render their existing wiki/code/<repo_page_slug>.md bytes.
compiler_and_page_integration.v2_material: Extend the source-aware compile-input successor with a closed code_relations group. Each relation references the complete observed v2 manifest/handoff set, config/capability evidence, accepted review and exact source association. The compiler validates refs and emits the relation.page_path deterministically.
page_policy: Do not overwrite an existing wiki/code page when a new commit/tree relation is accepted; use relation-specific versioned page paths and retain the old page in history.

A relation page must display relation_sha256, paper_id, repository, object format, commit_oid, tree_oid, source association, review decision, capability status, config evidence refs, and exact manifest/handoff refs.
Paper related links must be derived from accepted relation records and relation.page_path. Keep old repo_record.paper_ids links for legacy pages and add v2 links as additional rows.
Page bytes must remain NFC/UTF-8/portable and be included in collect_source_state's exact rendered-page comparison.
minimal_v2_compiler_changes: Add a code-v2 contract validator and a v2 code-page renderer alongside legacy._code.
Add a source-aware code relation group to the compile input schema and validate complete raw/source association/receipt refs before rendering.

Replace only the source-aware compiler's `for item in doc[code]: add(*legacy._code(item))` path with a dispatch that accepts a legacy group or a v2 relation group; do not alter legacy._code semantics.
Extend paper link derivation to include accepted relation page paths while preserving legacy repo links.
Add source_state v2 role documents and exact relation/ref closure checks before compile_pages returns.

required_checks: Extend _PREFIXES, _SCHEMAS, PATTERNS and _document without accepting arbitrary filenames. Each content-addressed path must match the exact document digest; each v2 manifest must bind one actual raw capture and code source-ledger row.

Add a v2 complete-set collector parallel to _legacy_artifacts/_code_groups. It must prove one observation commit/tree, exact requested ordinals, no target omission, one handoff/manifest per raw target, and relation refs that are all present and unique.
Extend _locators with a v2 branch that resolves code-locator.v2 only against v2 manifests. Continue rejecting repository Markdown claims in the legacy branch.

Extend _ancestry and _artifact_kind so v2 records, raw captures, manifests, configs, capabilities, reviews and relations receive source IDs, paper/relation owners, referenced/derived status, and coverage rows.
Extend preserve_history so old v1 repos, claims, source identity fields, relation pages and source-ledger snapshots cannot be replaced; relation changes are additive successor writes.
source_state_and_source_version_integrat.source_version_rule: source_versions.associate_source at lines 44-88 creates/reuses an immutable paper source association only after raw/head/receipt/ledger proof. Code relation source_association must copy an exact association reference plus digest. A changed paper source association, display decision, repository, commit, tree, target set, path, raw bytes, config parser profile, or relation review creates a new code observation/handoff/relation lineage. derive_display_heads at lines 144-177 chooses an explicit display chain and must never retarget an old code relation.

catalog_integration.compatibility: Do not widen source-catalog.v1 schema, KEYS, PROFILE, resource digest, cache parser, or legacy source-catalog-v1 query result in place. A v2 profile and resource manifest must carry the new row groups and a distinct catalog digest.
row_bindings: Every row includes exact artifact path and SHA-256, paper_id/repository/relation identity where applicable, source association ID/digest, source IDs, and receipt/head basis.
Capability and locator rows include exact resolution state and bounded excerpt/line metadata; unresolved or normalized-only evidence is explicit and cannot be silently dropped.

Coverage adds relation/artifact states such as relation_reviewed, relation_unreviewed, code_capture_registered, code_capture_unregistered, code_derived_referenced, and code_derived_unreferenced with deterministic reason codes.
catalog_integration.resolver: Keep source_catalog_projection._code_match/_code_resolution at lines 91-121 as the v1 resolver. Add `_code_v2_match`/`_code_v2_resolution` that require relation_sha256, manifest_sha256, handoff_sha256, exact Git fields and raw bytes; no heuristic path or excerpt lookup.
catalog_integration.reconstruction: source_catalog._perform at lines 44-71 must continue to audit and reconstruct current state before cache status/lookup/query. Build is the only .work cache write; query/lookup/resolve must refuse absent or stale v2 cache with the v2 catalog digest.

backup: Ensure every v2 artifact is under a managed .raw/derived namespace and appears in receipt writes. Ensure every code capture is either a receipt write or an exact captured raw claimed input. This satisfies backup_manifest.py:122-141's authorized_raw == actual_raw complete-set rule.
Retain relation/review/config/capability/manifests in the archive. They are semantic evidence, not disposable cache files; do not put them under .work.
Keep source_anchor equal to the current head receipt SHA-256. backup_archive.py:41-62 and 122-171 must continue to validate the embedded manifest, exact member set, modes and bytes.
restore: verify_restored_tree must compare the v2-inclusive manifest and source anchor before semantic checks.

restore_verification.verify_restored_vault currently calls the legacy catalog_store status/query/report at lines 12-24. Add a source-catalog-v2 current/status/query/coverage check and require all relation/manifests/config/capability/review row identities and catalog digest to match the restored bytes.
Restored relation pages and source evidence must pass audit_integrity, strict lint and exact compiler/state closure; a structurally valid ZIP is not sufficient.

must_remain_byte_compatible: legacy canonical_compiler._code and legacy page path
refusals: A v2 observation with a 64-hex commit cannot be coerced into v1 by truncating, rehashing, or changing the declared repository.
A normalized web/README excerpt cannot create a raw Git-verified manifest, source-ledger code capture, or official relation.
A partial target set cannot publish a complete relation; all missing/inaccessible/unsafe targets remain in observation coverage.
A code relation cannot inherit officiality from repo name, same organization, dependency/baseline link, display head, or model suggestion.
A new code relation cannot mutate an old repo record, alignment, source association, claim, page, receipt, or catalog row.
legacy_and_refusal_policy.legacy_projection: A 40-hex v2 observation may receive an explicit legacy projection only if it independently satisfies every v1 manifest/locator/repo/alignment condition and a deliberate compatibility adapter records the v2 relation as its source. The adapter must not fabricate PDF evidence or claim that v1 carries Git tree/blob proof.

implementation_order: Freeze successor schemas, path patterns, digest domains, source association join and versioned page policy.
Implement pure v2 validators/resolvers and adversarial fixtures first; keep v1 validators untouched.
Add source_state role/inventory/ancestry/complete-set closure and compiler dispatch.
Add one receipt-backed source-publication code-registration branch and inspect-time transaction/read-set checks.
Add v2 catalog profile/projection/query and backup/restore closure; only then expose commands.
non_goals: No GitHub/API fetcher, clone, archive download, shell command, recursive traversal, model loader, or weights download in public Python.
No automatic human officiality decision or relation publication from an observation alone.
No direct real Vault mutation, vpwiki-admin installation, network call, or connector invocation by this design artifact.

acceptance_cases: A 64-hex Git SHA-256 commit/tree/blob observation succeeds only through v2; v1 rejects it without truncation or substitution.
One retained observation/session proves a complete same-commit multi-file target set; directory replacement or cross-lineage responses refuse before handoff.
Repository, object format, commit, tree, path, mode, Git type, blob, raw bytes, normalized bytes and source_id mismatches each retain both sides and refuse publication.
CRLF raw bytes preserve raw_sha256 and Git blob proof while normalized_sha256 and line metadata use the existing UTF-8/LF rules.
Duplicate content at distinct paths remains two logical targets, two manifests and two locator origins.
Normalized-only, missing, inaccessible, unsafe, partial and stale targets cannot become complete source evidence.
Config imports, constructors, tags, anchors, interpolation, scripts, duplicate keys, unknown extensions and parser-limit overflow are rejected without execution.
Officiality shortcuts fail; a direct reviewed release without reverse backlink can retain an explicit evidence gap; third-party reproduction cannot become official.
A new source association, display decision, commit/tree, target set, config profile or relation review creates a new immutable relation and leaves old source evidence/pages/catalog rows unchanged.
A code publication's receipt claims raw captures and writes every derived artifact; audit_integrity, current source state, compiler page bytes, source-catalog-v2 and backup manifest agree.
Restored trees pass source anchor, receipt audit, strict lint, v2 catalog current/query/report and relation complete-set checks.
Legacy v1 fixtures and source-catalog-v1 fixtures remain byte-identical and resolve only through their original v1 paths.
Zero-egress and no-real-Vault-write sentinels pass for validation, handoff, publication prepare/inspect, catalog reconstruction and backup/restore verification.
open_gates: Architect must freeze exact successor schemas, path patterns, digest domains, source-publication payload shape, and allowed implementation/test paths before Builder writes.
The source-catalog worktree is dirty WIP without an exact-head acceptance; this advice is an interface review, not acceptance of that WIP.
Actual official repository trials, connector observations, human relation review and all real-data gates remain open and cannot be represented by this artifact.
